title: Animal Detection on Railway Tracks
tagline: Real-time YOLOv11 vision system for railway track safety.
description: A real-time object detection system using YOLOv11 to detect animals on railway tracks, with a focus on fast inference and reliable detection performance.
problem: Animals entering railway tracks can create serious safety risks, requiring fast and reliable object detection for timely identification.
solution: Developed and deployed a YOLOv11-based real-time object detection system for identifying animals on railway tracks, optimized for fast inference and evaluated on an external validation set.
contribution: Built the object detection pipeline, prepared and evaluated the model using Roboflow, and focused on balancing detection accuracy with real-time inference performance.
results: Achieved 90.1% mAP@50 on the external validation set
Achieved 90.4% precision and 83.9% recall
Achieved an F1 score of 87.1%
Deployed YOLOv11 Object Detection (Fast) for real-time inference

title: Employee Turnover Analytics
tagline: Predicting employee attrition and identifying high-risk employees with machine learning.
description: An employee turnover prediction system combining exploratory analysis, clustering, class balancing, classification models, and probability-based employee risk segmentation.
problem: Employee attrition can be difficult to identify early, making it challenging for organizations to understand turnover patterns and prioritize retention efforts.
solution: Built an end-to-end employee turnover analytics pipeline using exploratory analysis, K-Means clustering of employees who left, categorical feature encoding, SMOTE-based class balancing, and multiple classification models evaluated with ROC-AUC.
contribution: Performed EDA and turnover pattern analysis, segmented departed employees using K-Means, engineered model-ready features, addressed class imbalance with SMOTE, trained and compared three classifiers, and developed probability-based employee risk zones with retention strategies.
results: Random Forest achieved the highest ROC-AUC of 0.994655, outperforming Gradient Boosting at 0.985736 and Logistic Regression at 0.815429
Identified employee turnover patterns using satisfaction level, evaluation, project count, and workload indicators
Segmented employees into Safe, Low, Medium, and High turnover-risk zones using predicted probabilities
Converted model predictions into actionable retention strategies for employees at elevated risk of leaving

title: House Price Prediction
tagline: Advanced regression modeling for California house-price prediction.
description: An end-to-end house price prediction system comparing linear, regularized, and ensemble regression models with preprocessing, cross-validation, and XGBoost hyperparameter optimization.
problem: House prices depend on many numerical and categorical property features, making accurate prediction challenging without robust preprocessing and model comparison.
solution: Built a complete regression pipeline with missing-value imputation, numerical scaling, categorical encoding, 5-fold cross-validation, ensemble model comparison, and randomized hyperparameter optimization for XGBoost.
contribution: Performed exploratory analysis and outlier investigation, designed the preprocessing pipeline, implemented and compared multiple regression models, evaluated cross-validated RMSE, and optimized XGBoost through randomized hyperparameter search.
results: Compared nine regression approaches using 5-fold cross-validated RMSE
Evaluated linear, regularized, gradient boosting, and tree-based ensemble models within a consistent preprocessing pipeline
Performed randomized hyperparameter optimization across XGBoost tree depth, learning rate, estimators, subsampling, and regularization parameters
Analyzed fold-level performance to assess model stability and generalization

title: Predicting Natural Disaster Impact in Himachal Pradesh
tagline: Flood and landslide risk from multi-year weather data.
description: ML models predicting flood and landslide risk using multi-year meteorological datasets, with accuracy improved through feature engineering, preprocessing, and hyperparameter tuning.
problem: Flood and landslide risk in Himachal Pradesh needs to be anticipated from historical weather patterns rather than assessed after the fact.
solution: Built Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models on multi-year meteorological datasets, improving accuracy through feature engineering, preprocessing, and hyperparameter tuning.
contribution: Built the full modeling pipeline: preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and hyperparameter tuning for both models.
results: Analyzed 24,840 rainfall and temperature records across 12 districts of Himachal Pradesh
Engineered temporal features including previous-day rainfall, 7-day rolling rainfall, previous-day temperature, seasonal indicators, and temperature trends
Built a Rainfall Risk Classification model achieving 83.7% accuracy and 84.0% weighted F1-score
Developed a Rainfall-Temperature Risk Index (RTRI) to categorize conditions into Low, Moderate, and High risk levels
Created district-wise analysis to identify rainfall variability and temperature patterns for data-driven natural disaster risk assessment

title: Linear Regression Models From Scratch
tagline: California house-price regression, plus core ML algorithms built from first principles.
description: House price prediction using advanced linear regression (OLS with gradient descent variants), alongside Ridge, Lasso, and Polynomial regression implemented from scratch.
results: Implemented Linear Regression from first principles using NumPy, including both Ordinary Least Squares and Gradient Descent optimization
Built Ridge and Lasso regression with regularization to demonstrate practical control of model complexity and overfitting
Extended the regression pipeline with Polynomial Regression to model non-linear relationships in house-price data
Compared multiple regression approaches to understand the trade-offs between model flexibility, regularization, and optimization methods
Developed the core algorithms without relying on high-level machine learning libraries, strengthening understanding of the mathematical foundations behind regression models

title: Library Management System
tagline: Backend system for managing books, members, and library operations.
description: A Python and MySQL backend system designed to manage core library operations including book records, member management, borrowing, returns, and database-driven library workflows.
problem: Managing books, members, and borrowing records manually can lead to inconsistent data and inefficient tracking of library operations.
solution: Built a database-driven backend system using Python and MySQL to organize library records and automate core book and member management workflows.
contribution: Designed the backend logic and MySQL database structure, implemented CRUD operations, and developed workflows for managing books, members, borrowing, and returns.
results: Centralized library records in a structured MySQL database
Implemented core CRUD workflows for efficient book and member management
Automated borrowing and return record management through a Python backend
Built a maintainable foundation for extending the system with additional library operations
